text: Proposition forty-three changes the vote threshold for
certain local taxes.
Court decisions allow voter-proposed special taxes to pass
by a simple majority.
Proposition forty-three would require two-thirds for those
voter proposals too.
The proposition does not set a new tax
rate or immediately cancel every existing tax.
It changes the hurdle future proposals must clear.
A voter might want broad agreement before a
dedicated local tax takes effect,
regardless of whether a council or a citizen
group proposes it.
Another voter could object that more than half
the community may support a service but still
be unable to fund it.
Yes raises the threshold for these voter-proposed special
taxes;
no retains the current majority route.
